dimensions: Provisional visualization assumptions in metres. Not measured, not surveyed, not a buildable footprint, a contractor area or a property boundary.
axes: Model x runs along the assumed road and y into the site from its symbolic frontage line; levels use an ASSUMED road datum. The supplied survey depicts north, but model coordinates have not been registered to its boundary or compass orientation.

parameterEvidence.interiorWallThickness: ASSUMED — walls are centred on their drawn centrelines

parameterEvidence.cutawayHeight: ASSUMED — cutaway section height above finished floor
parameterEvidence.plinthHeight: ASSUMED — finished floor above land level, kept separate from land
parameterEvidence.roofSlabThickness: ASSUMED — flat-roof appearance only, not a structural or waterproofing design

parameterEvidence.materials: Local CC0 Poly Haven maps; appearance only
parameterEvidence.doorLeaf: ASSUMED door leaf 40 mm thick with a 4 mm gap, architrave trim 70 mm wide standing 15 mm proud of each wall face, entirely outside the clear opening (the clear opening is the wall cut; with the leaf open at 90° the passage is the opening less 40 mm). Appearance and checking only; no door specification.

land.evidence: OWNER-ESTIMATED road-to-land rise 1.5–2.0 m; not surveyed

yardAboveLand.evidence: ASSUMED front garden at land level

carportFloor.evidence: Independent ASSUMED carport-floor parameter, separate from the garden (land) and the house finished floor. Two alternatives are compared; the active one drives the plan, the sections, the 3D scene and the checks.

options.label: A · V2.3 level
options.evidence: The V2.3 value: carport floor = land + 0.10 m (ASSUMED).

options.label: B · lower carport (candidate)
options.evidence: ASSUMED candidate level +1.20 m above the road datum (adjustable). Chosen so the climb is about 12% average / 15% steepest instead of 19% / 23% at land +1.75, and so the carport stays below the garden at every land level (0.30 / 0.55 / 0.80 m).

site.evidence: ASSUMED display and composition geometry. A survey scan supplies documentary area and a depicted boundary; model coordinates have not been registered to that boundary. No site fit is established.

terrain.evidence: The conceptual raised site is modelled only inside the symbolic boundary walls (to their centrelines, so the walls hide its edges). Nothing outside them is raised.

background.evidence: DISPLAY BACKGROUND ONLY: flat ground at the road datum around the conceptual site, kept separate from it. Neighbouring ground levels, buildings and boundaries are unknown and are not modelled.

leftWall.evidence: ASSUMED symbolic boundary wall beside the driveway; neighbouring ground level unknown.

leftRearWall.evidence: ASSUMED symbolic boundary between the utility wall and the rear wall.

rightWall.evidence: ASSUMED symbolic boundary of the CONCEPTUAL envelope, not a legal line.

rearWall.evidence: ASSUMED symbolic boundary of the CONCEPTUAL envelope, not a legal line.

landShape.descriptor: irregular four-sided outline depicted in supplied survey
landShape.evidence: IMAGE-OBSERVED — supplied survey scan reviewed 2026-10-29; replaces the earlier almost-square owner description as visual evidence. Exact side dimensions and bearings absent from supplied sheet.

site.display_evidence: DISPLAY BOUNDS ONLY: how much ground the viewer and plan draw. Not the parcel and not the planning envelope.

conceptualEnvelope.evidence: CONCEPTUAL near-square planning envelope: the outer faces of the symbolic boundary walls and the front face of the main wall. An ASSUMED composition frame so the compact trial can be drawn; it is NOT surveyed, NOT derived from the 20-perch estimate and NOT the parcel.

surveyEvidence.evidence: CONFIRMED — document transcription from owner-supplied survey scan, reviewed 2026-10-29; authenticity and on-site boundary verification not established.

frontage.evidence: Separate PROVISIONAL frontage components from the road inward: road edge, open roadside drain, raised retaining edge with the lower planting strip behind it (the planting edge meets the rear side of the drain), stone-base white main wall, raised garden. No verge band. Every position and size is ASSUMED; ownership of everything in front of the main wall is UNKNOWN (it may be road reserve).

roadEdge.evidence: ASSUMED edge of the carriageway; not measured

drain.evidence: ASSUMED open roadside drain beside the road edge (the Street View shows an open drain). Its size, depth, falls and capacity are unknown. Both crossings leave the channel open beneath them; nothing is placed inside it.

plantingStrip.evidence: ASSUMED lower planting strip behind the retaining edge, in front of the main wall. Its soil surface level is derived from the retaining edge (toe + visible face − soil drop). Planting placeholders only; interrupted by the driveway and the pedestrian route; never inside the drain. Not assumed to belong to the owner; not counted as garden.

mainWall.evidence: ASSUMED main frontage wall: stone-look base rising from the planting soil, white render above. It retains the raised garden (0.50–1.00 m above the soil across the land range); retaining design by qualified professionals is required.

raisedGarden.evidence: Front garden at land level behind the main wall (OWNER-ESTIMATED 1.5–2.0 m above the road).

retainingEdge.faceEvidence: OWNER-ESTIMATED — TO BE VERIFIED. CONFIRMED owner clarification (2026-10-22): the approximately 1 m is the VISIBLE retaining-face height, measured from the adjoining drain-side ground at its toe to the top of the retaining edge / capping.
retainingEdge.toeEvidence: ASSUMED: the adjoining drain-side ground (drain rear lip, crossing and bottom landing) is +0.10 m above the road datum.
retainingEdge.soilEvidence: ASSUMED: planting soil surface 0.10 m below the top of the capping (kept separate from the capping).
retainingEdge.evidence: ASSUMED raised retaining edge in front of the lower planting strip, as in the owner feedback image (a stone/laterite-look face directly behind the drain with planting above) and REF-AERIAL/REF-PLAN. Conceptual appearance only: no structure, foundation, reinforcement or drainage detail is specified.

driveway.evidence: ASSUMED open driveway rising from the road to the carport. The 9.0 m climb (y 1.0 to 10.0) is unchanged from V2.1–V2.3; its rise depends on the active carport option. The gate stands on the level apron at its start. The right retaining wall stops at y 8.72 where the carport-to-garden stair passes.

carport.label: Carport (covered; level depends on the active option)
carport.evidence: ASSUMED: integrated covered carport on the left of the house. Position, footprint and 5.60 m depth unchanged from V2.3. The canopy roof level is RETAINED in both options (underside land + 2.80 m, as in V2.3: 2.70 m above carport A); in B the clear height above the lower floor is larger (headroom reported). The roof is carried by its own columns, separate from the gate piers.
carport.columnsEvidence: ASSUMED roof columns (visual only: no structural design). Independent of the gate piers. The right column stands against the end of the house wall so the carport walking route can pass it.

gate.evidence: Position and type PROVISIONAL. The gate stands on the main front-wall line at the foot of the driveway. Its base is derived from the driveway surface at that line, not from the raised garden or the carport floor. With the verge removed only 1.00 m of apron lies inside the wall line. Opening, leaf, ground clearance and the required space of each operating option are computed from this data; none is declared workable.

options.label: Sliding leaf, pocket to the right
Sliding leaf, pocket to the left

gate.verdict: NOT DEMONSTRATED — required spaces and conflicts are shown; no operating option is declared workable
gate.flagsEvidence: Every conflict computed by geometry-v2.js gateStudy() at land 1.50 / 1.75 / 2.00 must be flagged here, or the checks fail.

steps.evidence: ASSUMED straight flight beside the ramp as in REF-FRONT, rising from the bottom landing (y −1.20…−0.20, level with the drain-side ground) to the garden. The riser count follows the land level (risers of at most maxRiser); the flight end, the upper landing and the start of the garden path are derived from it. No stair-compliance, handrail, lighting or step-free check.

route.evidence: One connected pedestrian route from the road: crossing → bottom landing → flight → upper landing → garden path → porch steps → porch landing → entrance. Only the crossing level, landing depths, path turning points and widths are data; every join is derived from the flight and the porch steps and checked by tools/check-v2.mjs at land 1.50, 1.75 and 2.00 m and at each riser-count change point.

crossing.evidence: SCHEMATIC slab over the open drain at the flight's width; span, supports, capacity, levels and authority permission are NOT designed.

bottomLanding.evidence: ASSUMED landing between the crossing and the first riser, flush with the drain-side ground (toe level); with the verge removed it is cut into the strip zone and enclosed by the flight side walls. On land of unknown ownership.

upperLanding.evidence: ASSUMED level landing at garden level at the top of the flight; an optional pedestrian gate would sit here (REF-AERIAL/REF-PLAN/REF-FRONT-2 show one; REF-FRONT does not).

path.evidence: ASSUMED garden path. It starts at the far edge of the upper landing and ends at the foot of the porch steps (both derived); only the two turning points are data. Level with the garden.

garden.evidence: ASSUMED planting placeholders only, not a planting design; existing trees and overhead services are unknown. The compact V2.3 garden is kept (not larger); lawn 2 starts 1.10 m farther in because the street-route flight reaches farther into the garden. Beds, shrubs, palms, trees and pots are kept off both walking routes (checked).

walls.note: Master bedroom west wall beside the porch
Wall between the carport and the living room / kitchen (carport side)

openings.label: Dining side window onto the carport (moved from y 11.90 so the wall can take the TV; privacy to be reviewed)
Laundry window in the utility hall (was the kitchen window)
Utility window beside the stair (fixed, toughened — guarding TO BE VERIFIED)
Back door (moved 0.0325 m east to stay at the stair-foot lobby with the 0.90 m half-landing)

facade.evidence: Front-elevation relationships taken from REF-FRONT and checked against the plan by tools/check-v2.mjs

roof.evidence: ASSUMED flat roof slabs with a parapet, for appearance and the roof-removal cutaway only; not a structural, waterproofing or drainage design.

pv.evidence: INDICATIVE FUTURE PV after initial construction (R14/R15); layout, orientation, structure and upper-floor conflict unresolved.

stairTower.evidence: ASSUMED stair tower over the stairwell (roof access for PV maintenance; the future upper floor would continue from the same landing). Height, structure and waterproofing are not designed.

railing.evidence: ASSUMED steel safety railing on the main-roof parapets (as in the reference aerial); not a guarding design.

views.evidence: Cameras: position [x, height above the road datum, y] and target [x, height above the finished floor, y]. Presentation only. frameFreeArea frames the whole site inside the part of the window not covered by the controls and panels. plan / planSheet = Plan-view and SVG-sheet extents. aerial = oblique view of the whole site: target [x, y], direction, sphere radius that must fit.

unresolved.evidence: Items that must stay visible until professionals and measured evidence close them

items.title: Vehicle gate: space and operation
items.text: The gate stands on the main front-wall line, its base derived from the driveway surface. Sliding right meets the pedestrian entrance and the wall; sliding left runs beyond the symbolic boundary; outward swing sweeps the drain crossing and a waiting car; inward swing shows a clear footprint but is not declared workable (vehicle clearance, ramp surface and automatic operation are unchecked).

items.title: Waiting car outside the gate
items.text: With the verge removed only 1.585 m lies between the closed gate and the road edge; a waiting car stands on the drain crossing and projects about 2.9 m into the carriageway (display width, not measured). Automatic opening shortens the wait but does not create waiting space. Not resolved.

items.title: Drain crossings (schematic)
items.text: The driveway and the pedestrian route both cross the open roadside drain on schematic slabs that keep the channel open; span, supports, capacity, levels and authority permission are unresolved.

items.title: Ownership of the frontage strip
items.text: The verge geometry is removed but the uncertainty stays: whether the retaining edge, the planting strip, the apron and the bottom landing in front of the main wall belong to the parcel is unknown; they may be road reserve.

items.title: Retaining edge and excavation
items.text: The visible retaining face is about 1.0 m (OWNER-ESTIMATED — TO BE VERIFIED). Structure, foundation, drainage, the toe against the drain and the real levels are not specified. The lower carport (B) needs excavation and retaining against the raised garden; drainage and flooding of the lowered pad are unchecked.

items.title: Carport level A vs B
items.text: A (V2.3 level) keeps the 19%–22% climb; B (lower) reduces it but adds garden steps and a longer service stair. Neither is a vehicle-clearance, drainage or retaining finding.

items.title: Carport walking route
items.text: The route is stepped (not step-free). The walking strip shares the passenger door-opening space, the landing stands proud of the ramp edge, and the service stair may intrude into the driver-side door zone (all flagged). Handrails, lighting and a pedestrian gate are not designed.

items.title: Survey area received — site fit still unverified
items.text: The supplied survey states 0.0452 ha = 452 m² and prints 17.87 perches. Its north arrow and irregular boundary are documentary evidence, but no dimensioned side lengths, bearings, coordinates or spot levels are supplied. The rectangular viewer envelope remains an ASSUMED composition frame, not the parcel; no setbacks or site fit established.

items.title: Stair in the utility room: compliance and structure
items.text: The half-turn stair (18 risers of about 178 mm, 220 mm going, 0.90 m flights) is drawn geometry only. Rise, going, width, headroom, handrails, the stairwell opening, the half-landing and the stair tower need design and verification against the applicable Sri Lankan regulations by qualified professionals.

items.title: Stair tower and PV — orientation not registered
items.text: The survey depicts north, but the concept has not been aligned to it. Solar paths, neighbouring shade and PV performance remain untested. Stair-tower shading, waterproofing, maintenance and relocation for a future upper floor require design.

items.title: Rear service yard on an unverified strip
items.text: The yard uses the 1.1 m rear strip of the CONCEPTUAL envelope; its landing is about 0.87 m deep (less than 0.90 m). Rear boundary, drainage, canopy structure and access along the strip are unverified.

items.title: Utility window beside the stair
items.text: Kept as fixed toughened glazing with a 1.50 m sill (owner default); guarding beside the lower flight is TO BE VERIFIED.

items.title: Half-landing 0.90 m; rear landing 0.87 m remains flagged
items.text: Current half-landing 0.90 m equals or exceeds the 0.90 m flight width; the stored 0.855 m wording describes the earlier revision. Rear landing 0.87 m remains below the provisional 0.90 m target. This corrects an annotation only: stair compliance, headroom, guarding, structure and the rear boundary remain TO BE VERIFIED.

items.title: Open living/hall: structure and future floor
items.text: W-LIV-E is removed in the concept only. Whether it supports the roof slab or a future upper-floor wall is unknown; a beam, column or other support must be designed by a qualified structural engineer. Gross floor area does not increase.

items.title: TV wall and moved side window
items.text: The TV stands on the carport-side wall; the side window W-LIV-W moves 2.0 m toward the rear to light the dining area. Glare from the front glazing is side-on; carport privacy for the window is unresolved.

items.title: Laundry open to kitchen, dining and stair
items.text: Washer and laundry sink stay in the stair / utility hall, now openly connected to kitchen and dining. Keep dirty laundry, splash, detergent storage and washing noise controlled; fixtures are not moved in this pass. The back door, carport door and future upper-floor stair share this circulation.

items.title: Removed service partitions — structural review required
items.text: W-UK, W-UH and W-KD are removed from this new-build concept by owner selection. Roof and future upper-floor support across these lines require coordinated structural design. No beam, column or existing-wall removal is specified. Laundry fixtures and plumbing positions remain V2.9.

items.title: Back-door landing 0.87 m (depends on the rear strip)
items.text: The landing outside D-UB is as deep as the 1.1 m rear strip of the CONCEPTUAL envelope allows (0.87 m between the house wall and the rear boundary wall). Reaching 0.90 m needs about 0.03 m more strip depth, i.e. a survey and a boundary/setback decision; it is not obtained by moving the boundary in the model.

items.title: Open kitchen / utility — smell, noise and two-person use
items.text: Owner selected open kitchen, utility and dining connections for V2.10, superseding the earlier closed-kitchen trial. Hob extraction beside bedroom 3, outdoor discharge and replacement air still need design. Cooking smells and washer noise can now reach dining/living and the future stair. Sink/hob standing envelopes still overlap; this is not comfortable two-cook validation.

items.title: Pantry capacity still incomplete
items.text: The tall pantry removed in V2.8 is not reinstated by opening the partitions. Existing base and overhead storage stays unchanged; capacity, safe reach, fridge ventilation and mounting remain unverified.

compaction.evidence: The V2.3 compact garden is preserved. Parent values are computed from the V2.3 dataset by tools/check-v2.mjs, which fails if they drift or if the garden grows.

carportRoute.evidence: ASSUMED carport-to-house walking route: parked car → walking strip beside the car (passenger side, at carport level) → level landing → derived steps through an opening in the driveway retaining wall → upper landing at garden level → garden path along the house front → west porch steps → porch → entrance door. It avoids the sloping driveway except for the level landing at its top edge. The number of steps follows the level difference and the riser rule. The external route is stepped and is NOT step-free; nothing here is a stair-compliance or accessibility check (the indoor route to both bathrooms stays level).

service.evidence: ASSUMED raised service landing against the carport–utility door (level with the utility floor) and a stair along the left wall, derived from the level difference. It stays out of the parked-car envelope; it may intrude into the driver-side door-opening zone (flagged).

paramEvidence.doorOpening: ASSUMED practical car-door opening space beside the car (0.70 m)

paramEvidence.walkY1: ASSUMED north edge of the garden walk (kept clear of the right column)
paramEvidence.proudTolerance: a landing standing more than this above the ramp surface is flagged

carportRoute.flagsEvidence: Every finding computed by geometry-v2.js carportStudy() for options A and B at every test land must be flagged here, or the checks fail.

scaleFigure.label: 1.70 m person
scaleFigure.evidence: ASSUMED average adult height 1.70 m (owner request 2026-10-22). Scale reference only: not a person measurement and not a design clearance. It stands in the carriageway in front of the pedestrian route (the road itself is a display width, not measured).

stairDesign.evidence: ASSUMED half-turn stair geometry: risers derived from the floor-to-floor height and maxRiser; going 0.22 m (owner default Q1, 2026-10-23). Rise, going, width, headroom, handrails and the opening/landing structure are TO BE VERIFIED against the applicable Sri Lankan regulations by qualified professionals; no compliance is claimed.

canopy.evidence: ASSUMED light translucent canopy; structure and drainage not designed. Raised from land + 2.35 m (first V2.5 build, below the back-door head) to land + 2.70 m so it clears the heads of the back door (+0.15 m) and the utility window (+0.05 m) in the rear wall below it (owner instruction 2026-10-23).

serviceYard.evidence: ASSUMED covered rear service yard on the 1.1 m rear strip of the CONCEPTUAL envelope (not a surveyed depth): landing at floor level outside the back door, steps derived from the plinth, paving at land level for drying; washer and sink are indoors in the utility hall. Rear boundary, drainage and access along the strip are unverified.

usability.title: V2.10 provisional usability screen
usability.evidence: PROVISIONAL design criteria of this study, chosen to catch furniture or door changes that make a doorway, a work position or a service route unusable. They are NOT legal limits, NOT accessibility checks, NOT ergonomic studies and NOT building-code checks. Dimensions are ASSUMED model values; nothing is surveyed.
usability.claims: No accessibility, ergonomic or code compliance is claimed.

criteriaEvidence.approachDepth: PROVISIONAL: a free strip 0.60 m deep, as wide as the clear opening, on BOTH sides of every ordinary door (not only the swing side). At least routeWidth of it must stay free.
criteriaEvidence.workDepth: PROVISIONAL: 0.90 m of free standing space in front of a sink, hob, preparation counter, fridge or washer.
criteriaEvidence.routeWidth: PROVISIONAL: a 0.70 m wide swath along a service route, with the leaves of the doors it passes open at 90° (a 0.75 m opening leaves 0.71 m).
criteriaEvidence.headroom: PROVISIONAL: 2.00 m on routes and approach strips (the stair soffit above the half-landing and upper flight is tested).
criteriaEvidence.chairPull: PROVISIONAL: 0.60 m behind each dining chair.

reviewed: Half-landing deepened to 0.90 m (declared S1r2). Back-door landing 0.87 m kept and flagged; it depends on the rear strip depth (survey / boundary decision).
2026-10-29: partitions and doors removed by owner selection; route coordinates and all criteria retained.

wallStorage.evidence: ASSUMED occasional-use overhead storage; 0.20 m above generic fridge. Ventilation and reach need actual appliance/cabinet design.
ASSUMED wall cupboard over base landing, not over hob. Fixings, cabinet/hob clearances and usable shelf capacity TO BE VERIFIED.

stepFreeToBathrooms.evidence: CONFIRMED owner answer (INFO08): every enclosed ground-floor room reaches the common bathroom and the ensuite through rooms on the same finished-floor level. The check is level-only: door widths, turning space and wet-room falls are not checked.

drawing.evidence: Provisional dimension chains drawn on the plan sheet (wall centrelines). Chosen with the dataset so they follow the house block.
